'''Frank Harmsworth Allen''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry|FRSC]] [[CChem]] (1944&ndash;2014) was an internationally recognised [[crystallography|crystallographer]].<ref name=FrankAllenObituary>{{cite web|title=University of Cambridge|url=http://www.ch.cam.ac.uk/news/dr-frank-allen-frsc-cchem-1944-2014|accessdate=24 February 2015}}</ref>

==Biography==
Frank Harmsworth Allen was born in 1944 in [[Reading, Berkshire]] and raised in Pangbourne, a village 6 miles away and close to the River Thames. He was the only child of George W Allen and Gwendolen Retta (née Whittamore).

He gained a First in chemistry and a PhD in crystallography at [[Imperial College London]], and in 1968 moved to Vancouver to take up a post-doctoral fellowship, working with James Trotter<ref>{{cite web|title=James Trotter|website=The University of British Columbia|url=https://www.chem.ubc.ca/james-trotter|access-date=11 August 2023}}</ref> at the [[University of British Columbia]].<ref name=RobinTaylorObit>{{cite web|title=Obituary by Robin Taylor|url=http://journals.iucr.org/b/issues/2014/06/00/me0559/me0559.pdf|website=Acta Crystallographica Section B|accessdate=24 February 2015}}</ref> Before long, they had established the structure and conformation of thalidomide.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Allen|first1=F H|last2=Trotter|first2=James|title=Crystal and molecular structure of thalidomide, N-(α-glutarimido)-phthalimide|journal=J. Chem. Soc. B|date=1971|pages=1073–1079}}</ref>

A little earlier, in the [[Department of Chemistry, University of Cambridge]], [[Olga Kennard]] had founded the [[Cambridge Crystallographic Data Centre]]. She invited Frank Allen to join the group. He began in 1970, becoming Scientific Director and then executive director before retiring in 2008 and taking on the role of Emeritus Research Fellow.<ref name=RobinTaylorObit /> Initially, in his new role at Cambridge, Allen turned his attention to data and data processing, using the Cambridge Structural Database (CSD). He worked with W D Samuel Motherwell and others “to write the programs that turned the CSD from a data library into a scientific instrument”.<ref name=FrankAllenObituary/>

==Appointments and awards==
*Won the [[Royal Society of Chemistry|RSC]] prize for Structural Chemistry in 1994
*Gained the [[American Chemical Society|ACS]] [[Herman Skolnik Award]] in 2003
*Visiting professor of Structural Chemistry at the [[University of Bristol]]
*Member of the International Advisory Board of the PDB (RCSB)<ref>{{cite web|title=RCSB PDB Advisory Committee|website=RCSB PDB Protein Data Bank|url=https://www.rcsb.org/pages/advisory-committee|access-date=7 August 2023}}</ref>
*Member of many commissions and committees of the [[International Union of Crystallography|IUCr]]
*Member of the Council of the [[European Crystallographic Association]]
*Vice President of the [[British Crystallographic Association]] from 1997 to 2001
*Member of the Board of Lhasa Limited
*Member of the editorial board for [[Springer Publishing]]'s ''Structural Chemistry'' journal.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Hargittai|first=István|title=Frank Allen (1944–2014), member of the Editorial Board of ''Structural Chemistry''|journal=Structural Chemistry| volume=26|page=637|date=2015}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Robin Taylor, CCDC Emeritus Research Fellow, noted that{{blockquote|Frank was a sportsman. He played cricket for his county at school level and opened the bowling for a strong University Chemical Laboratory team. A desire to play cricket was one of his stated reasons for wanting a return home from Canada! He was a mainstay of [[Sawston]] hockey club … He sustained frequent injuries, including a broken nose, as is always a possibility when several men in close proximity to one another wave heavy sticks and propel hard spheres at high speed.<ref name=RobinTaylorObit/>}}
He also had a dry sense of humour:
{{blockquote|'''Retino-rectal Connexions'''

SIR, &ndash;Dr Robertson (''Nature'', '''233''', 435;<br />
1971) refers to an annoying visual<br />
condition which he calls tunnel vision.<br />
Surely he means hindsight?
{{indent|10}}Yours faithfully,
{{indent|15}}F. H. ALLEN
{{indent|15}}N. W. ISAACS

''University Chemical Laboratory,''<br />''Lensfield Road,''<br />''Cambridge CB2 lEW''<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Allen|first1=F H|last2=Isaacs|first2=N W|title=Retino-rectal Connexions|journal=Nature|volume=234|page=426|date=17 December 1971}}</ref>}}

Frank married Sandra J Newman (Sandy) in 1966. They had three children: Ashley, Andrew and Stuart. Ashley was killed in a road accident in 1988, aged 20.

Frank Harmsworth Allen died on 10 November 2014.  His funeral took place on the 27th at [[Histon#St Andrew's, Histon|St Andrew's, Histon]].<ref name=FrankAllenObituary/> He was then buried at Histon and Impington (Mill Road) Cemetery.<ref>Parish Clerk, Histon & Impington Parish Council, 14 August 2023</ref>
[[File:Frank_Harmsworth_Allen_Grave.jpg|250px|thumb|none|<div style="text-align: center;">Gravestone in Histon</div><div style="text-align: center;"> and Impington Cemetery</div>]]
